name: radical2

states.label: Read the board
states.description: Choose a plan from present board facts. Initial read plus at most two rereads on a line. Tried plans are skipped on the same board.

in_check.definition: The side to move is in check.

low_material.definition: The combined non-king material is at most 20 points (P=1,N=B=3,R=5,Q=9).

pawn_endgame.definition: No knights, bishops, rooks or queens remain.

material_up.definition: The solver has a positive non-king material balance.

material_down.definition: The solver has a negative non-king material balance.

check_available.definition: At least one legal move gives check.

capture_available.definition: At least one legal capture is available.

our_piece_attacked.definition: A specified friendly non-king piece is geometrically attacked.

our_passer.definition: A specified friendly pawn has no opposing pawn ahead on its own or an adjacent file.

our_pawn_near_promotion.definition: A specified friendly pawn is on its seventh rank.

mate.definition: The resulting side to move is in check and has no legal move.

capture.definition: The move captures an enemy piece, including en passant.

capture_piece.definition: The captured piece is a knight, bishop, rook or queen.

capture_higher.definition: A non-king captures a piece of strictly greater material value. Kings are incomparable, not zero-value attackers.

capture_equal.definition: A non-king captures a piece of equal material value.

capture_undefended.definition: The captured piece had no geometric defender before the move.

capture_defender.definition: The captured piece geometrically defended another enemy non-king piece before the move.

capture_checker.definition: The move captures a piece that was checking the moving side.

recapture.definition: The move captures the piece that made the immediately preceding capture; the setup move supplies history at ply one.

king_escape.definition: The king makes a legal move out of check.

block_check.definition: The mover interposes on a checking slider ray and resolves the check.

move_attacked.definition: The moving piece was geometrically attacked before moving.

piece_unattacked.definition: The moved piece is not geometrically attacked in the resulting position.

piece_defended.definition: The moved piece has at least one geometric defender in the resulting position.

piece_capturable.definition: The opponent has a legal immediate capture of the moved piece. This does not establish a sound sacrifice.

attack_piece.definition: The moved piece geometrically attacks an enemy non-king piece.

attack_loose.definition: The moved piece attacks an enemy non-king piece with no geometric defender.

attack_higher.definition: A moved non-king attacks a more valuable enemy non-king piece.

attacks_queen.definition: The moved piece attacks an enemy queen.

attack_defender.definition: The moved piece attacks an enemy piece which defends another enemy non-king piece.

attack_pinned.definition: The moved piece attacks an enemy non-king piece absolutely pinned in the resulting position.

fork.definition: The moved piece attacks at least two enemy non-pawn pieces, including the king when applicable. Geometry alone does not prove both threats are effective.

open_line.definition: The move uncovers a new attack by another, stationary friendly slider against an enemy piece.

skewer.definition: The moved slider attacks a more valuable enemy piece in front of a less valuable enemy piece on the same ray; the king ranks highest.

pin_king.definition: The moved slider newly absolutely pins an enemy piece to its king.

defend_attacked.definition: The moved piece defends a friendly non-king piece that was geometrically attacked before the move.

defend_loose.definition: The moved piece defends a friendly non-king piece that had no geometric defender before the move.

restricts_king.definition: The move reduces the enemy king's legal adjacent destinations, excluding castling.

king_toward_pawn.definition: The king reduces its Chebyshev distance to at least one pawn that remains on the board.

king_centralizes.definition: The king reduces its Chebyshev distance to the nearest of d4,e4,d5,e5.

opposition.definition: The king move leaves the kings on one rank or file with exactly one empty square between them.

block_passer.definition: The moved piece occupies the square immediately in front of an enemy passed pawn.

advances_passer.definition: The moving pawn was a passed pawn before moving.

underpromote.definition: A pawn promotes to a rook, bishop or knight rather than a queen.

connect_rooks.definition: The move newly puts two friendly rooks in direct rank or file contact.

mate_threat.definition: After a non-checking move, passing the opponent's turn would allow the mover a legal mate in one on the unchanged placement. This is a threat, not a forced-mate proof.

block_attack.definition: The moved piece interposes on an enemy slider's previously open attack on a friendly non-king piece.

creates_passer.definition: A moving pawn becomes passed when it was not passed before.

support_passer.definition: The moved piece geometrically defends a friendly passed pawn.

control_promotion_square.definition: The moved piece geometrically controls an enemy pawn's promotion square.

capture_passer.definition: The move captures a pawn that was passed before capture.

centralize_piece.definition: A non-pawn, non-king reduces its Chebyshev distance to the central four squares.

piece_more_mobile.definition: The moved non-pawn, non-king has more geometrical destinations not occupied by friendly pieces than before. Pins are not included in this mobility count.

enemy_mate_threat.definition: If the solver passed, the opponent would have a legal mate in one on the current placement. This does not prove a forced mate.

prevents_mate_in_one.definition: Before the non-evasion move the opponent had a mate in one under a pass test; after the actual move the opponent has no mate in one.

pin_piece.definition: The moved slider creates a relative pin to a more valuable enemy non-king piece.

unpin_piece.definition: Removes the absolute or relative pin of another friendly piece which remains in place; no other geometric absolute/relative pin of that piece remains.

king_toward_promotion.definition: The king reduces its distance to the promotion square of a passed pawn.

legal_move.definition: The supplied move is legal. Explicit fallback only: no adequate explanatory label has been selected.

material_improved.definition: The solver's current P=1,N=B=3,R=5,Q=9 material balance exceeds its balance at the initial puzzle FEN. A gain is not necessarily a positive balance.

quiet.definition: The opponent is to move, is not in check, has at least one legal move, and has no legal check, capture, or promotion. This narrow reply-quietness test does not rule out quiet threats or positional compensation.

surplus_covers_largest_legal_capture.definition: The solver's positive material balance exceeds the value of the largest piece the opponent can legally capture immediately. It ignores later tactics and promotion gains; it is not a win proof.

capture_attacker.definition: The move captures an enemy piece that, before the move, geometrically attacked at least one friendly piece (including the king).

attack_attacker.definition: The moved piece newly attacks an enemy piece that, before the move, geometrically attacked a friendly piece.

promotion_threat.definition: After a nonchecking move, the mover would have a legal pawn promotion if the opponent passed. This is a promotion threat, not a forced-promotion proof.

surplus_covers_attacked_material.definition: The solver’s positive material lead exceeds the sum of the values of all its geometrically attacked non-king pieces. This is an inventory bound, not a forced-win proof.

enemy_check_available.definition: The opponent has a legal checking move on the present placement (hypothetically passing the solver’s turn if necessary). Current check against the solver also sets this alarm.

enemy_advanced_passer.definition: An opposing passed pawn is on its sixth or seventh rank, at most two advances from promotion. Blocked or controlled promotion is not by itself a permanent stopping certificate.

capture_prior_target.definition: The move captures a target named by the preceding solver move’s attack inventory, following that target if the opponent moved it. This is a witnessed continuation of the plan, not a score or solution lookup.

forced_reply.definition: The resulting position has exactly one legal move for the side to move. Legal enumeration is not a claim that the forcing move is sound.

enemy_promotion_available.definition: The opponent has a legal promotion on the present placement (hypothetically passing the solver’s turn if necessary).

_terminal_stalemate.definition: The side to move has no legal move and is not in check.

attacks_passer.definition: The moved piece geometrically attacks an opposing passed pawn in the resulting position.

blocks_opposing_pawn.definition: The moved pawn ends directly in front of an opposing pawn on the same file.

controls_passer_path.definition: The moved piece controls an empty forward-file square of an opposing passed pawn.

keeps_opposition_geometry.definition: Both kings remain unmoved in rank/file opposition with one empty intervening square.

king_can_capture_mover.definition: The opponent has a legal king capture of the moved piece.

king_defends_rook.definition: The moved king geometrically defends a friendly rook in the resulting position.

moved_pawn_unopposed_on_file.definition: The moved pawn has no opposing pawn ahead on its file in the resulting position; captures are included and adjacent sentries may remain.

supported_unopposed_advance.definition: A solver pawn unopposed on its file has an empty immediate forward square geometrically defended by a friendly unit. Two related observations with the same pawn witness.

supports_pawn_advance.definition: The moved piece defends an empty square immediately ahead of a friendly pawn.

wing_pawn_majority.definition: The solver has more pawns than the opponent on at least one fixed half: a-d or e-h.

connected_rooks.definition: Two solver rooks geometrically defend each other.

king_has_flight.definition: The solver king has a legal adjacent destination.

opposite_bishop_ending.definition: Exactly one bishop on each side, on opposite colors; no knight, rook or queen.

king_guards_next_two.definition: A solver king controls the next two empty advance squares of a non-rook passed pawn.

enemy_passers_blockaded.definition: At least one enemy passer exists and every enemy passer is physically blocked on its next square by a solver non-pawn unit.

passer_exposed.definition: At least one solver passer is geometrically attacked and undefended.

edge_king_barrier.definition: The enemy king is on an edge file, same rank as the solver king, with one file between them.

single_clear_majority_candidate.definition: Exactly one non-rook candidate on a solver-majority wing, unopposed on its file but not yet passed, with an entirely empty forward file. Subsequent candidate observations use this same unique witness.

candidate_exposed.definition: A solver candidate is attacked and undefended.

candidate_advance_ready.definition: A clear-file candidate has an immediate advance square which is unattacked or defended by the solver.

candidate_beyond_king.definition: A clear-file candidate lies on the opposite side of the solver king from an edge-confined enemy king.

enemy_king_blocks_passer.definition: An enemy king physically occupies the next square of an enemy passed pawn.

king_distance_exceeds_pushes.definition: For a clear-file candidate the enemy king distance to promotion exceeds the pawn push count. Distance observation only, not a race theorem.

queen_only_heavy.definition: Enemy has at least one queen but no rook or knight.

rook_shelter_corridor.definition: Solver king and rook on own back rank; the rook guards an empty horizontal route to a corner with a friendly pawn immediately in front.

compensated_piece_attacks.definition: Each attacked solver non-pawn is defended or each attacker is sole defender of an attacked enemy countertarget of at least equal value.

material_lead_minor.definition: Solver material inventory balance is at least three.

king_guards_rook_now.definition: The solver king geometrically defends a friendly rook on this board.

promotion_trade_margin.definition: Balance remains positive after any legal capture of the newly promoted piece, counting a geometrical unpinned nonking recapture at the same square.

counterchecks_land_on_controlled_squares.definition: Every legal opponent checking move ends on a square already geometrically controlled by the solver. This does not assert that taking the checker is legal or sufficient, nor that every check is a refuted move.

king_supports_next_two.definition: Moved king controls the next two empty advance squares of a friendly non-rook passed pawn.

king_on_home_two_ranks.definition: Solver king is on its first or second rank.

rook_pawn_screen.definition: A friendly a- or h-pawn is on its second rank, screening a back-rank corner.

material_lead_queen.definition: Solver material inventory balance is at least nine.

king_rook_supported_file.definition: A solver king on its third rank and rook on its first rank share a file with an empty intervening square controlled by the king.

attacks_king_shelter.definition: The moved unit directly attacks an enemy pawn adjacent to the enemy king.

material_lead_rook.definition: Solver material inventory balance is at least five.

multiple_own_pawns.definition: The solver has at least two pawns.

all_attacked_pawns_defended.definition: Every currently geometrically attacked solver pawn has at least one friendly geometric defender.

king_to_edge_file.definition: The king moves from a non-edge file onto the a-file or h-file; no safety is inferred.

execution_notes: One card per chess plan; card choice never chooses a source policy.
Source study selectors are integrated into the existing material, multipurpose, defense and endgame plans.
All search and test limits unchanged. Positional completion rules are inherited bounded recognizers, not universal chess theorems.

All anonymous selection gates removed. Parent-position requirements are written directly on each selector. An observed zero undefended-piece capture count preserves unknown-observation safety. No budgets, stops, Oracle facts, card transitions or candidate ordering were changed.
